evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We piloted the Chitetezo antenatal iron-folate adherence package in 4 districts of Malawi. At the first antenatal visit a Health Surveillance Assistant (HSA) gives a 15-minute counseling session with a picture card; at 4 weeks the HSA makes one home visit with a pill count and leaves a reminder calendar. Our NGO trained and supervised the HSAs together with the district health offices. The scalability assessment says 'promising, test first': (1) HSA-delivered counseling without NGO supervision still raises adherence, to be tested in 2 new districts over 6 months; (2) the picture cards can be printed and distributed through the government supply chain. The Ministry of Health's Reproductive Health Directorate (RHD) has asked in writing for national roll-out through the HSA cadre across 28 districts. The national budget year starts in July; our donor funds us for 18 more months. HSAs report to district health offices, and HSA supervisors cover 25 to 40 HSAs each. The RHD director is the champion; the nutrition unit is wary because it runs its own IFA supply program. National elections are in 2 years. Please write the scale-up strategy.
evals.expected_output: A scale-up strategy in the output template that walks all nine steps and ends in an operational plan whose every line has an owner and a date.
assertions: Lists the program's parts, including training and supervision, each marked essential or not.
Fills the vertical-scaling table with each change marked yes, no, or unknown.
Gates the second wave of districts on the open test of counseling without NGO supervision.
Gives the resource team's role an end date within the 18 months of funding.
Every line of the operational plan names a role in an organization as owner and has a date.
Does not shorten the counseling or drop the pill count.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Help us scale our iron-folate adherence program nationally in Malawi.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the scalability judgment, the program's parts, the organization that would run it, and the environment, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks whether anyone has judged whether the effect will survive scale.
Asks for every part of the program, including training and supervision.
Asks who would run it routinely and whether they have asked for it.
Asks about the budget cycle or the policy environment.
Does not produce a strategy or an operational plan.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our donor wants the Chitetezo iron-folate package national across Malawi within 12 months. The Ministry of Health has not formally asked: the RHD director likes it, but the Secretary for Health has not seen it and the nutrition unit has not been consulted. Also, to make the home visit worth it at scale we want HSAs to dispense the iron-folate tablets during the visit, which the current Pharmacy and Medicines Regulatory Authority rules do not allow for HSAs. Our scalability assessment says 'promising, test first'. Write the strategy.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes what it safely can, makes securing a written request and the regulatory question the first actions, and tells the user to bring in a policy specialist and the ministry's planning and legal staff.
assertions: States that the user organization has not asked for the program.
Marks law or regulations as a change needed for HSA dispensing.
Puts securing a written request from the ministry before any training or expansion wave.
Tells the user to consult a health-systems or public-policy specialist and the ministry's planning and legal staff.
Does not write a plan that assumes HSAs may dispense tablets.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: To fit the HSAs' workload at scale we are cutting the Chitetezo counseling from 15 minutes to 5 and dropping the pill count at the home visit. Is that still the same program?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the question is whether changes to the program are allowed, and points to the skill that checks changes against the program's essential parts.
assertions: Says the request is about changing the intervention, not planning the scale-up.
Does not produce a scale-up strategy.
